call_sites:
reckon/cli.py — the follower's own source: tests/test_follower_checks_its_owner.py binds FOLLOWER_SOURCE as Path(cli.__file__).resolve() and the cases arm and observe the `crew follow --project

--session --no-color` command line it runs
reckon/crew/resumption.py:896 and :975 (the sweep that writes swept_by_pid, the first-wait-pass record the readiness barrier _wait_until_looping waits on)
reckon/crew/runs.py:1608 FOLLOWER_FRESHNESS_SECONDS = 1.0, consumed at reckon/cli.py:1754, the reload poll cadence the case's SETTLE_SECONDS derives from

reckon/crew/routing.py _register_session_member / _session_member_id — the per-session roster commit tests/test_crew_dispatch_arming.py now performs serially before its racing section (the same private helper tests/test_member_registration_commits.py:95 already calls)

findings.text: "Six named ids, each observed failing under load and passing alone before repair" is unsupported for two of the six. tests/test_crew_dispatch_arming.py::test_dispatch_restarts_a_producer_after_its_predecessor_dies and tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py::test_a_dispatch_under_the_shared_fixture_arms_no_producer appear in no FAILED line in any of the run record's 100 log files (grep '^FAILED' across them returns 11/4/4/3/3/2 occurrences for six other ids and zero for these two; the only places either name occurs are the dispatch prompt and the stream), and the node's loaded runs pass both 3 of 3. test_watch_arming_isolation.py is byte-identical to base at head, so id 6 received no repair. The dispatch's done-when required EACH id be "first observed FAILING under load AND PASSING ALONE, with both logs recorded". The measure itself still holds — all six pass three consecutive loaded runs, which I reproduced independently — but the sentence describes observations that were not made.

baseline_suite's "The three owned files fail under a loaded -n 8 run for the six named ids" is unsupported for the same two ids, for which no failure log exists anywhere in the run record, and its "Each named id passes when run alone at base" is contradicted by the node's own logs/solo-follower-* logs, a serial base run at 3d61f106 reporting "2 failed, 3 passed" on the two follower ids — so the base-failure evidence generalises to four ids of six, and is intermittent even for those. The manifest's checkpoint line repeats the six-id claim.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified 4 production call site(s) — the stamped follower source and its `crew follow` command line (reckon/cli.py), the sweep that publishes swept_by_pid (reckon/crew/resumption.py:896, :975), the reload poll cadence the wait bounds derive from (reckon/crew/runs.py:1608, consumed at reckon/cli.py:1754), and the roster-provisioning path the dispatch-arming case now calls serially (reckon/crew/routing.py _register_session_member)
item_verdicts.diff: Read all four commits against base 3d61f106: git diff --numstat 3d61f106 c6dce87b lists exactly seven paths and no others. f8751c48 replaces the single 2.0 s owner-exit wait with a reload-then-exit two-phase wait in tests/test_follower_checks_its_owner.py; 91e3fd05 adds the swept_by_pid readiness barrier (_wait_until_looping), the content append and the serial roster provisioning; 91b8f1d7 adds the fcntl.flock source-mutation window and the xdist_group markers; c6dce87b lands the plan paragraph, the archive anchor and the figure. No reckon/ file changed, no test deleted, no skip or xfail added or removed (test counts per owned file identical at base and head: 5/2/6/8).
item_verdicts.done_when: The head half is met and I reproduced it: 13 passed twice in my own scratch tree at c6dce87b under a genuine concurrent -n 8 full-suite run of the main checkout (logs rev-mine-a/b.log), with the watched third file carrying only its two pre-existing failures, and the source left byte-identical to head (residue check clean); the declared negative control also reproduces — moving the source change before the barrier fails the case with "the follower did not replace its image". The reproduction half — each id "first observed FAILING under load and passing alone, with both logs recorded" — is met for four ids of six; for test_dispatch_restarts_a_producer_after_its_predecessor_dies and test_a_dispatch_under_the_shared_fixture_arms_no_producer no failure log exists and the record nonetheless claims all six were so observed (findings).
item_verdicts.goal: The landed change is the repair the goal names. The reload ordering is fixed at its mechanism — the cases now wait for the sweep's first wait pass (swept_by_pid) before changing the source and change content rather than mtime alone, so the change lands after the baseline is fixed — and the roster contention is removed from the case by provisioning both session members serially before the racing section. At head all six ids pass three consecutive -n 8 runs of their files under a concurrent full-suite load, twice independently reproduced by me, and the property each case pins is intact (no bound deleted, no assertion weakened; the one bound change, EXIT 2.0 → a measured 3.0 for the post-reload exit, is documented with its three measurements 1.193–1.240 s at tests/test_follower_checks_its_owner.py:106–113 and the failing direction it still catches).
item_verdicts.manifest: Every figure it states that I re-ran reproduces — the three loaded head runs, the serial run, the residue claim, and the declared mutation — and its negative_control_note discloses the arming mutation's non-reproduction rather than claiming it. Its test_logs paths resolve and its gate command is the one its logs ran. Two of its statements overreach: baseline_suite generalises base failures to six ids where four have any log and says each named id passes alone at base where the node's own serial base log reports two failures (findings).

justifications.durability: The repair is structural: the readiness barrier waits on the observed condition (swept_by_pid) rather than a sleep, the trigger is a content append so size and mtime both move, the edit window is an fcntl.flock exclusive across processes (xdist_group is inert under the default --dist load, which the worker proved), and both call sites restore bytes and timestamps under try/finally, so a failing assertion inside the window still restores. The one relaxed bound is documented with its measurements and the unbounded failing direction it must still catch. It fails as it should: the declared mutation reproduces "the follower did not replace its image". Deduction: two of the six ids were never observed failing for any cause, so for them nothing shows the case can still fail when the property breaks.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced the head claim myself — 13 passed twice under a genuine concurrent -n 8 full-suite load with the third file carrying only its two pre-existing failures, cli.py byte-identical to head afterwards — and the declared mutation reproduces at head with the same failure message the worker's control logs carry; the worker's control blocks cover three of four causes with the arming mutation's non-reproduction disclosed. But the load-failure half of the record is thin where it is widest: two of the six ids the dispatch required be seen failing under load appear in no failure log at all, the plan landing record and the manifest checkpoint both claim all six were so observed, and baseline_suite's "passes alone at base" is contradicted by the node's own serial base log. Reconstructing which content the three loaded runs measured required reading the worker's stream edits (the final file mtimes are the control restores, and the restores compose to identity with head) because the loaded logs carry no revision header.
justifications.fit: The new helpers sit in the files' own idiom: named module constants with the measurement behind each bound in the comment beside it (EXIT_WITHIN_SECONDS 2.0 with its twenty-pass rationale, SETTLE_SECONDS derived from runs.FOLLOWER_FRESHNESS_SECONDS, RELOAD_EXIT_WITHIN_SECONDS 3.0 with its three measured values), docstrings that name the mechanism and the direction each wait must catch, explicit failure messages carrying the argv observed, and pytest.mark.xdist_group rather than ad-hoc serialisation. The one reach into a private product helper (routing._register_session_member) matches an existing call at tests/test_member_registration_commits.py:95. Naming checks over the added lines return no true hit — the only matches are matplotlib/CSS colour literals and the SVG DOCTYPE.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The delivered change does what the goal names: the two real causes are repaired at their mechanism (baseline-fixed-before-change via the swept_by_pid barrier plus a content append; serial roster provisioning before the race), no test is skipped, xfailed, deleted or weakened, and all six ids pass three consecutive loaded runs of their files, which I reproduced twice under genuine external load. Deduction: the record's own account of the goal's reproduction step — every id seen failing before repair — is true for four of six and asserted for six in three places, so the landing describes more of the mandated process than was performed.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff 3d61f106 c6dce87b changes exactly the seven declared paths — the four test files, the figure and its script, and the two cumulative documents — with no reckon/ file touched, no plan meta scalar altered, and the worktree clean at c6dce87b. The plan document is pure addition (+45/-0); the archive's only deleted line is the plan-commits meta it extends, and its anchors go 19 → 20 with no peer record displaced. test counts per owned file are identical at base and head (5/2/6/8) and no skip or xfail was added or removed; the declared write fence named test_watch_arming_isolation.py and it is left byte-identical to base, which the review records rather than holding against the node.
